issue.title: pthread library perhaps should be linked to libdronelink.a
issue.body:
Hi Julian, as we see that DroneLink is built as a [static library](https://github.com/PX4/DroneLink/blob/master/CMakeLists.txt#L52); why so ? Is it not meant to be used by multiple applications ?

And, `libdronelink.a` itself [uses threads](https://github.com/PX4/DroneLink/blob/master/core/udp_connection.h#L7); but it is not linked to pthread lib. The [example takeoff_and_land](https://github.com/PX4/DroneLink/blob/master/example/takeoff_and_land.cpp#L8) itself is using threads so linking thread make sense.
But if an application doesn't intend to use threads don't link it as part of their build; then app build would fail again for the same reason! 

Ideally, `libdronelink.a ` should be linked to pthread library. And, I think its not possible if its static library.
Please share your thoughts about this and correct me if I am wrong.

Thanks.
Shakthi

comments.body:
> Hi Julian, as we see that DroneLink is built as a static library; why so ?

The current build as a static library easily allows to build it for iOS and Android. I'm not sure if and how that is possible with a dynamic library.

> And, libdronelink.a itself uses threads; but it is not linked to pthread lib

It is linked to a thread library, check: https://github.com/PX4/DroneLink/blob/master/CMakeLists.txt#L12, however pthread does not get included into a static lib because [pthread seems to be part of glibc](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/10390584/force-gcc-to-static-link-e-g-pthreads-and-not-dynamic-link#answer-10390911).

I'm open for suggestions and changes but I need to understand what exacly the problem is. In my opinion, linking to pthread is possible.

issue.title: How to connect a drone using system id with mavsdk

repository.name: MAVSDK
repository.description: API and library for MAVLink compatible systems written in C++ 20

issue.body:
Hello Everyone,

I am using MAVSDK-Java to monitoring drones.
Currently, MAVSDK java only exposes to connect drones using UDP or TCP which is working perfectly.
Now, to connect with multiple drones, the app requires connecting using the system id which I am not able to do.

Later I came to know that the C++ library can do the task.
I have tried to build a C++ library  [here](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK.git) to use with Android, but I can't make a build due to some errors. followed as per the documentation.

So the questions are 
1. Can I achieve the above(connect the drone with system id) using C++ lib.
2. Can I get the .so file of this C++ lib so that I can use it in android through JNI.

FYR: @JonasVautherin @julianoes
